title: PLANING: A Loosely Coupled Triangle-Gaussian Framework for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
claim: A hybrid primitive-plus-neural representation reconstructs scenes online with both sharp geometry and high-fidelity rendering, and the result is usable downstream.
layout: Full-bleed render split into three wedges, with a capture inset top-left and a simulation inset top-right
description: A full-width indoor scene dominates the figure. The scene is a lobby with a wall of wooden grid cubbies spelling INNOVATION, plus sofas. The image is cut into three diagonal wedges. The top and main wedge is the photorealistic Neural Gaussians rendering. The bottom-left wedge shows the same scene as flat, beige and brown Planes. The bottom-right wedge shows a grey Triangles mesh with sharp edges. White curved labels sit on the seams. A grey inset at top-left shows a camera icon and a row of monocular input frames, with an arrow and the text 'Monocular Captures (126 views), TIME: 63.9s, PSNR: 35.30dB'. At top-right, a floating grey mesh of the extracted layout holds humanoid and quadruped robot figures, which stand for simulation and locomotion training. The eye goes first to the colourful wall render.
caption: PLANING introduces a loosely coupled triangle-Gaussian representation for streaming 3D reconstruction, balancing geometric accuracy, high-fidelity rendering, and computational efficiency. Compared with 2DGS-based representations, explicit edge-preserving triangle primitives provide sharper structural boundaries and more stable geometric learning, leading to improved geometric reconstruction quality. The extracted compact planar structures further support high-performance simulation environments for locomotion training in embodied AI. Project page: https://city-super.github.io/PLANING/.
abstract: Streaming reconstruction from monocular image sequences remains challenging, as existing methods typically favor either high-quality rendering or accurate geometry, but rarely both. We present PLANING, an efficient on-the-fly reconstruction framework built on a hybrid representation that loosely couples explicit geometric primitives with neural Gaussians, enabling geometry and appearance to be modeled in a decoupled manner. This decoupling supports an online initialization and optimization strategy that separates geometry and appearance updates, yielding stable streaming reconstruction with substantially reduced structural redundancy. Despite operating online, PLANING improves dense mesh Chamfer-L2 by 18.52% over the offline baseline PGSR, surpasses the streaming baseline ARTDECO by 1.31 dB in PSNR on average across the six evaluated datasets, and reconstructs ScanNetV2 scenes in 2.1 minutes, over 5x faster than offline 2D Gaussian Splatting while matching per-scene optimization quality. Beyond reconstruction quality, the structural clarity and computational efficiency of PLANING make it well suited for a broad range of downstream applications, such as enabling large-scale scene modeling and simulation-ready environments for embodied AI. Project page: https://city-super.github.io/PLANING/
